leadText:
Team Rocket's mechas refers to the many robots and machines Jessie, James, and have used in their wild schemes throughout and its adaptations. It is unknown how they get them–since they usually have little money–or how they are transported. The mechas first appeared in the second episode of , Pokémon Emergency!, with the debut of the Meowth Balloon. One-time mechas began to appear starting in The Kangaskhan Kid.

Typically, the mechas fail to accomplish their functions and are destroyed, some even before getting a chance to be used. The nomenclature of some one-time mechas, such as "Mark 2" or "Model 2", even suggests that previous versions of those mechas failed and had to be rebuilt. 

 was referred to as the brain behind the trio's mechas on a few occasions in .

 was referred to as the brain behind the trio's mechas on a few occasions in .

==In animation==
===Recurring mechas===
====Team Rocket's balloons====
===== Balloon=====
 

=====Others=====
 

====Team Rocket's submarines====
Alongside the Meowth Balloon, the trio also uses many submarines that serve as underwater transportation, and are powered by pedaling.

 

Sparks Fly For Magnemite (Internationally)

It was used as Team Rocket's main mode of transportation through the Orange Islands and made infrequent appearances after that all the way until . It returned in the , and in the in The Sinnoh Iceberg Race!, where it was slightly redesigned.

====Rocket Prize Master====
 

 A Poké Ball vending machine that dispenses Pokémon for Jessie and James to temporarily use. 

===List of mechas===
==== ====
Mechas were occasionally used in . However, they became more common in the .

 

===== Miscellaneous =====
Apart from the above, several robots looking like giant Pokémon made an appearance in 's theme park in the episode Island of the Giant Pokémon. They were not a part of any sinister plot, but instead were a business venture.

==== ====
Mechas were much more common in compared to in the .

 

The powerful and massive nature of the mecha makes it one of the most powerful and strongest that the Trio have ever owned, however, they would never get to properly use it after and a fall in and meddle around with it, showing its true power, enough to destroy an entire city and being strong against a majority of attacks used against it.

Eventually, uses to damage the mechanical controls, and uses to melt away the windows to let Togepi and Sentret free before it eventually explodes into flames.

Unintentionally, it ended up making a shortcut for people to get to Violet City through the drill going through a mountain.

This mecha reappeared in The Same Moon, Now and Forever!, where it was used to capture and in a net fired from its mouth. It was destroyed by Ash's Snivy's .

It is first powered through a power supply, which is soon destroyed by Gary's Umbreon's . It can also be powered using exercise-bikes to generate power, and if an Electric-type attack (like ) hits it without Counter activating.

The mecha is soon destroyed by Ash's Cyndaquil's , with Ash's Chikorita's trapping the counter doors to allow the fire inside the Mecha to cause it to explode.

==== ====
 

Robo 

 

A green version, known as the Mean-Green Stealing Machine, was used in On Olden Pond. This variant only features two grabber claws. This variant was destroyed by a stronger version of 's powered up with 's and 's , but caused it to crashland into everyone.

 

Noodle Nabber

It reappears in Noodles! Roamin' Off! under a different name; the Noodle Nabber, where Pikachu immediately destroyed it as soon as it captured him.

 

Mecha Mountain King

 

==== ====
 

Has a cameo in Fighting Ire with Fire!

It was burned up by Hippowdon's .
